---
title: "Summarise values into new rows"
---

Numerical values can be summarised and displayed in dedicated rows. 
This is helpful to display observations alongside statistics in the table.
`SUMMARISE` can be repeated to compute multiple summaries.

## Clause syntax

```ggsql
SUMMARISE [GROUP | GRAND] <operation> OF <columns>, ...
  SETTING <parameter> => <value>, ...
```

Also accepts the spelling `SUMMARIZE`.

## Scope

```ggsql
[GROUP | GRAND]
```

The scope directly following the `SUMMARISE` clause determines which rows the operation aggregates over.
Setting the scope to `GROUP` will compute the summary for each group determined by `FACET` clauses separately.
The `GRAND` scope will compute the summary for all rows.
Without spelling out a scope,  the default will be `GROUP`.
When no groups are declared by `FACET` and the scope is set to `GROUP`, all rows are treated as belonging to the same group.
The difference between a `FACET`-less `GROUP` scope and a `GRAND` scope is largely a diffrence in style and label spanning.

## Operation

```ggsql
<operation>
```

This part of the clause can be an identifier or a string representing an expression.
When using an identifier, one of the following operations are available:

* Counting: `count`, `n_distinct`, `n_missing`.
* Totals: `sum`, `prod`.
* Extremes: `min`, `max`, `range` (max - min), `mid` (min + max) / 2.
* Centrality: `mean`, geometric mean `geomean`, harmonic mean `harmean`, root-mean-square `rms`, `median`.
* Dispersion: standard deviation `sdev`, standard error `se`, variance `var`, interquartile range `iqr`. Note `sdev`, `se` and `var` are population statistics, not sample statistics.
* Percentiles: `p05`, `p10`, `p25`, `p50` (median), `p75`, `p90`, `p95`.

When using a string as an expression, you can use any of the identifiers in curly braces.
For example `'{mean}'` will display the mean via expression.
The expressions can be used to display multiple metrics in a single cell, e.g. `'{median} ({p25}, {p75})'` will display the median and interquartile range in one cell.
Inside the brackets, you can use limited arithmetic.
The operands include the operation identifiers listed above (like `mean`, `sdev`), numeric literals (`2`, `0.5`) and scientific notation (`1e6`).
The `+`, `-` unary operators and `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` binary operators and `(`/`)` parentheses for grouping.
For example you can use `'({mean - 1.96 * se}, {mean + 1.96 * se})'` to display a 95% confidence interval (assuming normal distribution) in parentheses separated by a comma.

For the naked, non-string identifiers the formatting of the cell values is applied externally via `FORMAT` clauses.
The string expressions can be self-formatting via the same syntax as [scale breaks](scale.qmd#break-formatting).
All summary metrics are assumed to be numeric.
As such, the `:num` formatter is implied and does not need to be written out in full.
The expression `'{mean:%.2f}'` will display the mean with two decimal points in printf-style.
Other formatters can be used, e.g. `{max:bytes}` to display base-1024 size.
When using arithmetic, the formatting is placed at the end and is applied to the result so that `'{mean + sdev:%.2f}'` rounds the expression to two decimals.

## Column selection

```ggsql
OF <columns>, ...
```

The `SUMMARISE` clause requires a comma-separated list of columns to aggregate.
The columns must be part of the `TABULATE` selection.
Only the 'counting' operations listed above can be applied to columns of any type, the other operations require numeric columns.

## Settings

```ggsql
SETTING <parameter> => <value>
```

The `SETTING` sub-clause is typical with key-value pairs.
It currently takes the following parameters:

* `place`: the location of the summary rows relative to the body rows they summarise. 
Can be `'top'` to place the summary rows at the top of each group or table, or `'bottom'` (default) to place the summary rows after the body rows.
* `rowlabel`: A string for the label of the summary row. The default `null` falls back to printing the operation, where string expression operations are displayed without formatting details.
* `missing`: A string option for how to treat `null` values in the table. 
The default `'propagate'` will list any non-counting operation as `null`, and counting operations include null-rows. 
Can be set to `'drop'` to explicitly ignore `null` values in aggregates and ignore these rows in counting operations.

## Examples

A summary without groups will summarise all rows.

```{ggsql}
CREATE TEMP TABLE my_data AS 
SELECT DISTINCT ON (species, island, sex) * FROM ggsql:penguins
WHERE bill_len IS NOT NULL AND sex IS NOT NULL

TABULATE * FROM my_data
SUMMARISE mean OF bill_len, bill_dep
```

A grand summary will always summarise all rows, and is displayed with a stronger border.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
SUMMARISE GRAND mean OF bill_len, bill_dep
```

Groups can be specified using `FACET`.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
FACET island
SUMMARISE mean OF bill_len, bill_dep
```

The labels of summary rows compose with regular body row labels in the stub.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
FACET island
FORMAT STUB species
SUMMARISE mean OF bill_len, bill_dep
```

The display of the label in the stub can be changed using the `rowlabel` setting.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
FACET species
SUMMARISE mean OF bill_len, bill_dep
  SETTING rowlabel => 'Average'
```

The summary cells are subject to `FORMAT` when using plain identifiers, along with the body rows.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
FACET species
FORMAT bill_len, bill_dep RENAMING * => '{:num %.2f}'
SUMMARISE mean OF bill_len, bill_dep
```

To specifically format the summary values, you can use the expression string form.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
FACET species
SUMMARISE '📏 {mean:%.2f}' OF bill_len, bill_dep
```

You can use repeated summaries.
The order in which the summaries are declared determine the order of the rows.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
SUMMARISE p25 OF bill_len, bill_dep
SUMMARISE p50 OF bill_len, bill_dep
SUMMARISE p75 OF bill_len, bill_dep
```

Or display related summaries in a single cell.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
SUMMARISE '{p50:%.2f} ({p25:%.2f}, {p75:%.2f})' OF bill_len, bill_dep
```

When data contains 'null' values, they propagate to aggregate metrics (but not necessarily count metrics).
Notice how the summary of `bill_len` comes out as 'null'.

```{ggsql}
SELECT species, island, sex,
       CASE WHEN island = 'Biscoe' THEN NULL ELSE bill_len END AS bill_len,
       bill_dep, flipper_len, body_mass
FROM my_data

TABULATE *
SUMMARISE '{mean:%.2f}' OF bill_len, bill_dep
```

You can ignore 'null' values by using the `missing => 'drop'` setting.

```{ggsql}
SELECT species, island, sex,
       CASE WHEN island = 'Biscoe' THEN NULL ELSE bill_len END AS bill_len,
       bill_dep, flipper_len, body_mass
FROM my_data

TABULATE *
SUMMARISE '{mean:%.2f}' OF bill_len, bill_dep
  SETTING missing => 'drop'
```
